story.see: Our box covers the northern half of the lake. The open lake is black all season. From late July the western and northern shores brighten as the water edge pulls back; the 'when' layer dates this to August and September. On 18 October the pool south of the causeway brightens too, but one date cannot rule out wind.
story.physics: Lake Urmia is a salt lake with no outlet: it gains water from rivers and rain and loses it only by evaporation. Every summer it shrinks. Over decades, drought, river dams and pumping of groundwater for farms have cut its inflow, so the lake has shrunk dramatically and left wide salt flats.
story.lband: Calm brine mirrors L-band radar away and looks black in HH. Exposed mud and salt crust are rougher and send more signal back, so a retreating shoreline turns brighter. Caution: smooth, wet salt flats can also look almost as dark as water, so our water layer probably includes some wet flats at the edges.
story.people: Once about 6,000 km² and among the largest salt lakes on Earth, Lake Urmia had shrunk to 10% of its former size by late 2017, and NASA images showed it almost entirely dried up in September 2025. In 2018 trees were planted to slow the wind that carries salt particles from the exposed bed.

credits: NISAR GCOV preview images: NASA/JPL-Caltech and ISRO, distributed by ASF DAAC. Uncalibrated previews at about 180 m; values are display brightness, not backscatter.

steps: 1. Radar image before, 20 Jun–14 Jul (median of 3 passes, HH channel).
2. Radar image after, 19 Aug–12 Sep (median of 3 passes).
3. The difference: the echo rose by about 0.15 (0–1 brightness scale) inside a patch of about 297 km² of changed echo, summed over every changed patch in the frame.
4. A check: between 20 Jun–14 Jul, within the before group, the same pixels change by +0.02 on average, and 16 % of them cross the threshold, so the control is not clean.
5. It stays: the patch is still there on every later pass.

stats.area_label: area of changed radar echo, not a measurement of land cover, crop or forest loss
stats.unit_note: brightness units are the preview's 0-1 display scale; dB-like = 30 x brightness assumes a ~30 dB stretch (unverified)
stats.method_note: Preview brightness (uncalibrated, ~180 m), 3x3 boxcar + per-date gain normalisation; AFTER minus BEFORE (medians), 9x9 boxcar; threshold = median + 3.09 robust sigma of the same-signed change in a control built from two halves of a quiet interval (a Gaussian 99.9 % level that heavy tails do not inflate); connected patches of at least 10 km² kept, the one nearest the reference position (else the largest) reported. The area is the area of changed radar echo, not a measurement of land cover, crop or forest loss.
